title: Panasonic's Lumix SHX1 Is a 6K Box Cinema Camera That Records Blackmagic RAW to an SSD
summary: Panasonic announces Lumix SHX1 6K box cinema camera recording Blackmagic RAW
detailed: Panasonic announced the Lumix SHX1, a 6K box-style cinema camera weighing about 2.17 lb, scheduled for release in the US in January 2027.

The camera features a 24.1-megapixel full-frame sensor, 5-axis in-body stabilization, Phase Hybrid AF with 779 points, and records Blackmagic RAW directly via USB-C to an SSD up to 2 TB without an external recorder.
It supports internal Apple ProRes RAW recording to CFexpress Type B cards, records 4K 120p without time limits, and includes preinstalled ARRI LogC3 alongside V-Log.
Accessories launching with the camera include the AU-XHU1 XLR handle unit and AU-GRP1 control grip, with a live production module and firmware updates planned for the first half of 2027.
sentences: Panasonic's Lumix SHX1, due in the US in January 2027, is a box-style cinema camera with a 6K full frame sensor, in-body stabilization, phase-detect autofocus, and 12G-SDI in a body that weighs about 2.17 lb.
No earlier Lumix body could write Blackmagic RAW straight to a drive without a separate recorder, and this one also keeps Apple ProRes RAW on an internal card.

Panasonic calls the SHX1 "the first compact cinema camera in LUMIX history," and it draws on the two businesses Panasonic merged in 2024: the professional video side behind its VariCam cinema cameras and the consumer imaging side behind Lumix.
Inside is a 6K partially stacked full frame sensor of about 24.1 megapixels, with an optical low-pass filter to suppress moiré and false color.
In V-Log, Panasonic claims 15 stops with Dynamic Range Boost switched on and a little over 14 without it, though the boost mode trades away some image quality and ISO range and adds rolling shutter.
Raw comes two ways, and neither needs an external recorder.
Blackmagic RAW records over USB-C to an SSD of up to 2 TB, and the files open in DaVinci Resolve without conversion.
You can also select Blackmagic's color science to make matching easier when you're cutting alongside Blackmagic cameras.
While you record to the SSD, the cards can't take the same footage, though a proxy can go to an SD card.
Apple ProRes RAW HQ and ProRes RAW go to a CFexpress Type B card inside the camera, which keeps a gimbal or solo rig free of extra cables.
Recording the sensor's full 3:2 area in Blackmagic RAW caps out at 24 fps at 6K, with a slight crop.
The regular codecs go faster in that open gate mode, up to 30 fps at 6K or 60 fps at 5.1K, both in 10-bit 4:2:0, and Panasonic has also added a 48 fps mode at 3.8K in 10-bit 4:2:2.
ARRI LogC3 comes preinstalled next to V-Log, along with ARRI's Look Library, to help the SHX1 sit beside an ARRI A camera.
Panasonic notes that the ALEXA 35 uses LogC4 instead.
For handheld and gimbal work, the 5-axis in-body stabilization works with lenses that have no optical stabilization of their own, and Dual I.S.
2 adds a stabilized lens's correction on top of it at long focal lengths.
For walking shots, Active I.S. pairs with electronic stabilization, with a cropless electronic mode for wide angle lenses and an anamorphic mode that includes roll correction.

Autofocus is Phase Hybrid AF with 779 points, and Panasonic says its AI detection holds onto eyes and faces even when they're tilted or partly hidden, and keeps tracking a selected person when someone crosses in front.
The 3.0-inch, 1.84-million-dot touchscreen sits on top of the body and tilts up or swings out to the side, and the anamorphic desqueeze display now works for vertical framing too.
The aluminum and magnesium alloy body records 4K 120p without a time limit within its rated operating temperatures, using a large fan and a dedicated thermal system.
Outputs are 12G-SDI up to 4K 60p and full-size HDMI, with BNC timecode in and out plus timecode sync over Bluetooth.
Audio records internally in 32-bit float through the 3.5mm input, and the camera runs on Micro V-mount batteries that can also power accessories, both firsts for Lumix.
Cards go in dual CFexpress Type B and SD slots behind a locking door, and two locking USB-C ports handle the SSD and USB Power Delivery.
Two accessories arrive with the camera.

The AU-XHU1 XLR handle unit adds four channels of 32-bit float audio in combination with the body's 3.5mm input, plus 96 kHz/24-bit recording, and its XLR section and top handle separate for lighter builds.
The AU-GRP1 control grip attaches with an ARRI-standard rosette and carries white balance, ISO, and iris buttons, a joystick, and a zoom rocker for power zoom lenses.

Further out, Panasonic plans the AU-LPU1 for the first half of 2027, a live production module with genlock, a PoE++ network port, and IP control that lets its remote controllers and third-party pan-tilt heads drive the SHX1 as a PTZ camera.

A firmware update in the same window will add control of Tilta's Mirage variable ND and let a Tilta hand wheel run focus and iris on L-mount glass without external lens motors, and Panasonic says it's developing a power zoom lens for the camera.
Panasonic has built box cameras before, so the "first compact cinema camera" label depends on how you define the category.
The Micro Four Thirds BGH1 arrived in 2020, and the full frame BS1H followed in 2021 at $3,499.
Neither had a screen, and both sent raw over HDMI to an external recorder, such as Blackmagic's Video Assist for Blackmagic RAW.

The SHX1 keeps the cube shape and the mounting points but adds a monitor, a Micro V-mount plate, and raw recording without a recorder, which cuts out the external monitor and recorder those earlier cameras needed for raw work.
The price puts it above Panasonic's own hybrids.

At $4,699.99, the SHX1 costs about $1,500 more than the Lumix S1II, whose sensor has the same resolution and partially stacked design, so the premium pays for the cinema body around it: SDI, BNC timecode, the battery plate, and direct Blackmagic RAW recording.
It also sits about $800 above Canon's EOS C50, which records 7K open gate Cinema RAW Light internally for $3,899.
If you already shoot L-mount and need a B camera that matches an ARRI or Blackmagic A camera in post, the SHX1 is the more direct fit.
The SHX1 is available for preorder for $4,699.99, or $5,499.99 with the AU-XHU1 and AU-GRP1.
